result.title: ProAS: A Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping Framework for Multi-Turn Agentic Reinforcement Learning
result.summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) has emerged as the primary paradigm for optimizing Large Language Model (LLM) agents, yet efficient critic-free algorithms (e.g., GRPO) suffer from a fundamental uniform credit assignment dilemma that broadcasts trajectory-level advantages equally to all actions. Our analysis reveals that this uniformity inherently reinforces structurally invalid actions in preferred trajectories and ignores the downstream cascading influence of early pivotal deviations in unpreferred ones. To resolve this without introducing critic overhead, we propose Progress-Aware Advantage Shaping (ProAS), a plug-and-play framework that leverages a dynamically evolving Agentic Reference Graph (ARG) to achieve fine-grained credit assignment via Masking Unreasonable Incentives (MUI) and Asymmetric Penalty Redistribution (APR). Extensive experiments across Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct demonstrate that ProAS universally elevates mainstream group-based baselines to new state-of-the-art performance, achieving peak success rates of 91.9\% and 94.3\% on ALFWorld, alongside 66.7\% and 70.8\% on WebShop, respectively. Furthermore, it accelerates training convergence by up to $2.44\times$ while maintaining strong robustness against imperfect or distilled ARGs. Codes: https://github.com/LINs-lab/ProAS.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对多轮 LLM agent 强化学习中 GRPO 等无 critic 算法将轨迹级优势平均广播给所有动作的问题，提出 ProAS：用动态演化的 Agentic Reference Graph 做细粒度信用分配，通过掩蔽不合理激励与非对称惩罚再分配，在 ALFWorld 与 WebShop 上提升成功率和收敛速度。
AI.relevance_reason: 该方法关于步骤级信用分配与「早期关键偏差的下游级联影响」的处理，可能为 LVR 中 latent 推理步的贡献分配与监督信号设计提供可核查的线索，但论文面向纯文本 agent、不涉及视觉或 latent 状态，迁移需自行判断。
